runs.title: New Orleans tanker-cruise collision: what happened
runs.prompt: A tanker collided with a river cruise ship carrying more than 130 people near the Port of New Orleans, on the Mississippi River, reported on 13 November 2026. Find out what actually happened: how many people were on board, whether anyone was injured or missing, and what official sources (coast guard, local authority, the cruise line) are saying. Start from these pages and follow any links they reference. Report facts only, and name which source each fact came from.
runs.answer: What happened: at about 12:30 p.m. on Friday 13 Nov 2026, the tanker Atlantic Asphalt collided with American Cruise Lines' paddlewheeler American Heritage while the cruise ship was docked on the Mississippi at 1350 Port of New Orleans Place, near the Crescent City Connection Bridge — roughly two hours after it docked to begin disembarkation (Port NOLA, via WDSU and Newsweek). Aboard were approximately 129 passengers plus crew members, i.e. the "more than 130 people" figure (Port of New Orleans spokesperson, via Newsweek and WDSU); video showed the ship listing onto its side. On casualties, no official figure exists in the pages I read: Newsweek quoted Port NOLA saying "the number of injuries and the cause of the allision have not yet been confirmed," while WDSU reported (updated 2:02 p.m. CST) that rescues were under way for "at least 12 people who are still in the water" — so at least a dozen people were in the river, but no confirmed dead, injured or unaccounted-for count had been released. runs.answer: Per ESPN's Shams Charania (Nov 13, 2026), "Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray wants a trade from the franchise, and his agent, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul, and team officials have started working on a resolution" — i.e., a private, two-sided process rather than a public, adversarial trade demand. Murray himself has not made an on-record statement; his only public signal was since-deleted social-media posts after Wednesday's 145-111 home loss to Brooklyn, in which he fired back at a "social media coach" fan account over the team's record with and without him and alleged internal "sabotage" (per Yahoo Sports' headline that he "recently clapped back at fans on social media," and Fox News/ClutchPoints/HITC coverage of the deleted "sabotage" posts). No Pelicans statement or on-record team comment appears in any of the reporting I could read — NOLA.com's version attributes confirmation only to "a source," so the team's posture is described solely through Charania's anonymous sourcing: the front office is engaging directly with Rich Paul/Klutch to find a resolution instead of commenting publicly.

runs.title: Ronaldinho, 46, at Ravenna: first-start details
runs.prompt: Brazil legend Ronaldinho, aged 46, has come out of retirement to play for Italian Serie C club Ravenna, and is set for his first start. Find out the key facts: when is his first match, who are Ravenna playing, what are the details of his contract, and what Ronaldinho or the club have said about the comeback. State clearly what is confirmed versus rumour.
runs.answer: CONFIRMED: Ravenna FC by Cipriani (owned by Ignazio Cipriani, with partner Black Duck and Ariedo Braida on the management team) announced on 23 June 2026 at Cipriani Miami that Ronaldinho, 46, would be "officially registered as a player"; the club's own programme notes say he joined the squad in Italy on Friday 13 November, trained on Saturday and is available to coach Andrea Mandorlini for the Serie C derby against Forlì on Sunday 15 November 2026 at the Stadio Bruno Benelli — BBC reported he is set for his first start (he is also chasing a 300th career goal). Ronaldinho said: "New colours, same smile… I cannot wait to dance with the ball and write a beautiful new story with Ignazio Cipriani and the Cipriani family. Football has always been joyful for me, and I'm excited to bring that spirit to Ravenna. Let the magic begin!" Cipriani called it "an extraordinary moment for the club… he was my idol growing up". The club also announced a charitable component with Street Soccer USA; note that the widely cited "four-year contract" is Ravenna's technical/kit partnership with Nike, not Ronaldinho's playing deal. RUMOUR/UNCONFIRMED: no official length, salary or bonus figures were publish

runs.title: Pick the clearest New Orleans collision source
runs.prompt: You are judging which article most clearly and factually reports the collision between a tanker and a river cruise ship near New Orleans on 13 November 2026. Visit each candidate page and pick the single best source for the key facts: number of people on board, injuries or missing, and what official sources say. Consider readability (no paywall/login), how it attributes the facts, and how current it is. Explain your pick and note any candidates that were blocked or paywalled.
runs.answer: Best pick: ABC News' report ("Vessels collide near Port of New Orleans, prompting massive emergency response"). It gives the clearest headcount — about 129 passengers and crew aboard the riverboat American Heritage, attributed to the operator/officials rather than a bare claim — and it names its sources directly (Port of New Orleans statement, American Cruise Lines, the Coast Guard, and Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry's post on X), while stating plainly that the extent of injuries/what happened to everyone aboard was not yet clear and that search-and-rescue was ongoing. It was free to read and carried a same-day update timestamp. Runners-up: LiveNOW from Fox and Newsweek also carried the 129 figure with attribution (Newsweek to the cruise line, LiveNOW to local/institutional officials), and NBC News was vaguer ("more than 100," "nearly 130" via affiliate WDSU). The Guardian live blog is readable but gave only a loose "more than 130 people" and the mayor's office's "multiple rescued" line. Note: no accessible page confirmed any specific injury or missing-person count, so any firm casualty number should be treated as unconfirmed.

Google News RSS links redirect through a JavaScript-only interstitial, so the WDSU/FOX 8 stories were unreachable; FOX 8's own search page renders results via JavaScript only.

runs.title: Pick the best Alaska governor results source
runs.prompt: Alaska is one of several states still counting votes in the November 2026 midterms, and 'Brian Poindexter' is trending in connection with the Alaska Governor race. Visit each candidate page and pick the single best live-results source for the Alaska governor election: one that shows current vote counts/percentages and who is leading or has won, and that loads without a paywall or login. Explain your pick and note any candidates that were blocked or paywalled.
runs.answer: Pick: NBC News' "Alaska Governor Midterm Election 2026: Live Results" page (nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/alaska-governor-results). It loaded free, with no paywall or login, and showed live numbers: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins (D) 50.0%, Bernadette Wilson (R) 28.7%, Dave Bronson (R) 13.7%, with 252,140 votes counted, 87.9% of expected votes in (~35,000 remaining) and the race flagged "Too early to call" — i.e. a leader but no winner yet. Everything else I tried was blocked or dead: AP and Politico hit Cloudflare "Just a moment" walls (403), NYT and RealClearPolitics returned 403 JS/ad-block gates, CNN, Fox News, CBS, ABC and 270toWin all 404'd, Ballotpedia and Wikipedia returned no readable results, and the official Alaska Division of Elections results page was a hard 403. One caveat on the premise: nothing on the NBC results page or in a Bing search links "Brian Poindexter" to the Alaska governor race — the only candidates shown were Kreiss-Tomkins, Wilson and Bronson (with Treg Taylor appearing in district breakdowns), so that trending claim looks unfounded.
